source.title: Minimize Length of Array Using Operations

teaching.hint: What events permanently prevent the array from shrinking further?

solution_outline.decisive_insight: Each operation removes one array entry, but a zero is inert. A nonmultiple of the minimum can create a unique smaller value; otherwise copies of the minimum force residual zeros.
solution_outline.approach: Find the minimum `m`. If some value is not divisible by `m`, a sequence of positive remainders can reach length one. Otherwise count copies of `m` and return half that count rounded up.
solution_outline.state_and_invariant: When all values are multiples of `m`, no positive result below `m` can be created. Only a zero-producing operation can lower the count of `m` values, by at most two.
solution_outline.correctness: A nonmultiple permits a strictly decreasing positive minimum until a unique minimum remains, enabling a one-element result. In the all-multiple case, the minimum-copy bound forces at least `ceil(count/2)` residual items, and pairing minima after deleting larger values attains it.
solution_outline.pitfall: Treating zeros as still selectable incorrectly predicts that every input can shrink to length one.

common_wrong_turns: Use the gcd alone as the branch condition
Count multiples rather than copies of the minimum
source_fidelity_notes: The operand order, positive-entry requirement, and permanently inert zero are explicit.
